evals.name: missing-acceptance-criteria
evals.prompt: A corpus rule told you to open a follow-up issue for a bug you decided not to fix now. Your draft body is: 'The export button throws when the filename has a slash in it. Not fixing now.' You're about to run `gh issue create` with that body. Reply only; do not create the issue.
evals.expected_output: Add a `## Acceptance criteria` section with concrete, testable bullets before filing, since the issue is a response to a corpus instruction. State what closes the issue, e.g. the export button rejects or sanitizes a slash in the filename instead of throwing, with a bullet per testable condition.
assertions: Says the draft is missing a `## Acceptance criteria` section.
Says acceptance criteria are required because the issue is filed in response to a corpus instruction.
Gives at least one concrete, testable bullet rather than a vague restatement of the bug.
Does not create or submit the issue as drafted.

evals.name: reviewing-existing-issue
evals.prompt: The direct bot filed a GitHub issue with this body: 'Projection rebuild is slow for large event logs. Investigate and improve.' Review it for the required issue-filing format. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Flags the missing `## Acceptance criteria` section with concrete, testable bullets, and that 'investigate and improve' is not testable as written. Recommends adding a section with bullets stating an observable condition, such as a bounded rebuild time for a stated log size.
assertions: Identifies that the issue body has no `## Acceptance criteria` section.
Says 'investigate and improve' is not a concrete, testable closure condition.
Recommends adding bullets stating an observable, checkable outcome.

evals.name: ad-hoc-issue-not-mandated
evals.prompt: I want to file a quick personal reminder issue for myself, not tied to any corpus instruction or automated filing - just a note to self. Does it need an `## Acceptance criteria` section? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Not mandated: the acceptance-criteria format applies to issues filed because of an AI Corpus instruction (a direct bot, repository tooling, or a corpus-directed follow-up). An ad-hoc personal issue outside that context is not required to have it, though using the same format is still encouraged for consistency.
assertions: Says the `## Acceptance criteria` section is not mandated for this ad-hoc issue.
Explains the format applies to issues filed because of an AI Corpus instruction, not every issue.
Notes that following the same format is still encouraged for consistency, without making it a requirement.
